**Finding-triage ruling: Promote** — `finding` to `pm:queue`, scoped to the diagnostic widening.

Plugin-registered metadata types are exempt from the org-scope write refusal (protocol.ts:7740-7748, statically-declared types only) AND invisible to the cold-boot audit (:12230-12246 scans DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY only), so their org rows are skipped with neither refusal nor report. Widening the audit scan to the live registry is safe under all three of the card's readings and endorsed by the code's own doc note at :7737 (the warning is free and should be maximal). Refusal-widening stays out of scope.

This card was filed by this seat's own #6190 dispatch as an out-of-scope finding; promoted 2026-08-10T00:12Z under the maintainer's centralized finding-triage directive, **scoped deliberately to the diagnostic widening only**.

Carried into the dispatch as binding:

- **In scope**: widen the cold-boot audit's scan (`protocol.ts` ~`:12230-12246`) from `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` to the live registry, so a plugin-registered type's org-scoped rows are *reported*.
- ⛔ **Out of scope: refusal-widening.** The org-scope write refusal (`~:7740-7748`, statically-declared types only) stays exactly as #6190 landed it. Widening a refusal removes a capability and would extend a ruling measured over the static registry to a surface nobody measured; widening a warning does not.
- The asymmetry is not an oversight but the code's own stated posture — the doc note at `~:7737` says the warning is free and should be maximal, which is also how #6190's dev justified keeping `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows` (PR #6600) hatch-blind while the refusal honours the hatch. This card makes the audit live up to that note.

**No unmet promotion gate**: triage states the widening is safe under all three of the card's readings and points at the code's own endorsement, rather than deferring a measurement to the implementer.

Region: `metadata-protocol`'s audit region — disjoint from #7000 (`packages/metadata`), dispatched alongside it.

## os-dev report

**Issue** #6992 · **Status** `done` · **PR** https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/7154 (draft) · **Branch** `claude/issue-6992-audit-live-registry-scan` · **Base** `origin/main` @ `3e8e669c0` · **Premise still valid:** yes, verified against the base before implementing.

### 1. Boot-order measurement — the likeliest way this went wrong, and it did not

Instrumented `reportUnhydratableOrgScopedRows` and booted the real `app-showcase` app twice (ephemeral `--fresh` and a persistent `OS_HOME`; identical both times). At the instant the audit fires:

```
engine.registry.getRegisteredTypes() = ["action","analytics_cube","api","app","book","capability",
  "connector","dashboard","data","dataset","doc","email_template","flow","hook","job","mapping",
  "object","package","page","permission","report","sharing_rule","theme","view","webhook"]
metadataService present = true;  getRegisteredTypes() = <the 27 declared types only>
live \ DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY = ["analytics_cube","connector","data","package",
  "sharing_rule","theme","webhook"]     ← 7 types, incl. all 4 the issue names
```

**The accessor** is the pair `getMetaTypes()` already reads — `engine.registry.getRegisteredTypes()` plus the `metadata` service's `getRegisteredTypes()` — which I extracted as `listLiveMetadataTypes()` so the listing and the audit cannot drift into two vocabularies.

**Is it populated when the audit fires? Yes**, and the reason is structural: the kernel runs *all* plugins' `init` (Phase 1) before *any* `start` (Phase 2); manifests register into the SchemaRegistry during Phase 1 via `ql.registerApp`; the audit runs inside `loadMetaFromDb`, i.e. `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` Phase 2. **The widening is live, not inert.**

One sub-assumption of the card was **falsified and is worth recording**: the *metadata service* is not the source that carries this family at boot. `MetadataManager.typeRegistry` is seeded with `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` in the manager's **constructor**, and its artifact load (`MetadataPlugin.start`, ordered after objectql via `optionalDependencies`) has not happened yet — so early in boot it contributes exactly the declared set. The **SchemaRegistry** is what carries `theme`/`connector`/`webhook`/`sharing_rule`. I read both anyway, because both are what `getMetaTypes()` lists.

### 2. Flood count — two measured numbers, plus the structural bound

- **Unseeded real showcase boot:** `sys_metadata` holds **0 rows** (metadata comes from the artifact, not the DB) → **0 extra log lines**. 
- **With a seeded realistic corpus (22 rows):** still **exactly 1 line** — the widening adds 4 *segments* to the line that already existed, never new lines.

Structural bound: an org-scoped row can only be produced by `SysMetadataRepository.put` stamping `organization_id`, i.e. an authenticated Studio/API write under an active organization — precisely the population this warning targets. Combined with the one-aggregated-line shape and the 5-name-per-type sample cap, the worst case is *one extra segment per newly covered type*. **No flood.**

### 3. What I changed

| File | Change |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` — audit region | Scan = declared non-org-overridable types **∪** every live type the registry does not declare at all. JS-side re-check now also re-checks the *type* predicate (see below). Message reworded + `[plugin-registered]` marker. TSDoc gains an explicit divergence section. |
| same file — `getMetaTypes()` | Extracted `listLiveMetadataTypes()` (behaviour-equivalent) so listing and audit share one accessor. Declared-allowed deviation ("plus whatever accessor the live registry needs"). |
| `protocol.org-scoped-cold-boot-audit-live-registry.test.ts` | New, 9 cases. |
| `.changeset/cold-boot-audit-live-registry-scan.md` | `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch. |

⛔ **Refusal region (`~:7740-7748`) untouched** — the only occurrence of `orgScopedWriteRefusal` in the diff is a `{@link}` cross-reference inside my new TSDoc. `restoreArtifactRegistryView`, `assertSortFieldsExist`, `packages/metadata`, `packages/spec`, `content/docs/releases/` all untouched.

**On PM assumption 3 (report shape):** shape is unchanged — one line, same tag, same `type×count (names)` detail, same sample cap. Two **wording** changes were unavoidable and are the answer to "does this family need different wording to be actionable": (a) the old clause "types **the registry declares** NOT per-org overridable" is *factually false* for a type with no declaration; (b) the `[plugin-registered]` marker exists because the remediation differs — a declared type's org write is refused from now on, so its rows are residue that cannot grow, whereas an undeclared type's write is **not** refused and the same names return after every restart until the author stops.

**One extra change I want visible:** the JS-side filter now re-checks the *type* predicate too. Before the widening, `orgOverridable` happened to *be* that re-check (inside the declared registry, "not org-overridable" and "in the scanned list" are the same statement). After it they diverge — a type neither declared nor live (plugin uninstalled after the row was written) is not in the list — so without this line the TSDoc's standing promise *"the JS filter re-checks both"* would have become false.

### 4. Reverse verification — direction predicted before running, every category preserved

**A. Real boot, same seeded corpus, same `OS_HOME`, only the audit implementation swapped.** Reverted to **my own base** (`3e8e669c0`), never a moving `origin/main`.

- **BASE — predicted total=3, measured total=3:** `flow×2; object×1`. The 11 plugin-registered org rows are **absent** — #6992's defect, reproduced in a real boot.
- **WIDENED — predicted total=14 and still one line; measured total=14, one line:** adds `webhook×7 [plugin-registered]` (5 names + `+2 more`), `theme×1`, `sharing_rule×2`, `connector×1`; `flow×2`/`object×1` correctly unmarked.
- **Guards silent in BOTH directions, as predicted:** 3 org-scoped `view` rows (ADR-0005 design), 4 env-wide `webhook` rows (org predicate), 1 draft org-scoped `webhook` (state predicate).

**B. Unit level — predicted 4 RED / 5 GREEN, measured 4 RED / 5 GREEN. No missed predictions.** Reds fail in the shape that names the defect (`no [metadata_org_scoped_unhydrated] line in: []`, and a line containing only `flow×1` where the corpus has `flow` *and* `theme`).

**Honestly labelled: 4 of the 5 greens are guards, not evidence**, for four different reasons — the registry-entry premise reads the registry directly; two cases assert an *absence* that a deleted producer trivially satisfies; `degrades to the declared scan when the live accessor throws` has base behaviour *as its expected output*, so it cannot go red in reverse by construction (it guards against the widening becoming a boot failure, not against the widening); and `does NOT extend the write refusal` is green **because** the refusal is untouched — that is its purpose.

All 22 of #6190's own cases stayed green in the reverse run, so my reds are not bought by breaking theirs.

**Nothing was left unmeasured** — no prediction short-circuited.

### 5. Tests + CI

- New file: 9/9 pass. `metadata-protocol` full suite: **67 files / 861 tests passed**.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `metadata-protocol`: **63 errors — exactly the `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` ledger figure**, so this PR adds zero.
- 15 lint-job family gates run locally, all green (`check:meta-type-normalized`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:empty-changeset`, …).
- **CI: all 25 check runs completed, 23 `success` + 2 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate), zero failures.** Gate jobs by conclusion: **`ESLint` = success**, **`TypeScript Type Check` = success**, `Test Core` = success, `Build Core` = success, `Check Changeset` = success, `Dogfood Regression Gate` = success.
- `skip-changeset` **not applicable** — this PR ships a changeset and `Check Changeset` passed on its own.

### 6. Worth recording, not acted on

`getMetaItems({ type, organizationId })` merges org rows **without consulting `allowOrgOverride`** — an org row of *any* type is readable on demand. So the warning's claim "absent from the **process-wide registry**" stays literally true for the new family (process-wide consumers read env-wide), and it is *not* saying the data became unreadable. This is why the line is actionable rather than alarmist. No defect, no issue filed.

**Out-of-scope findings: none.** Nothing outside the card's surface warranted a filing.

Not marked ready, auto-merge not enabled — left for the PM.
